title: Protocol for isolation and characterization of lung tissue resident memory T cells and airway trained innate immunity after intranasal vaccination in mice
protocol: Anesthetize mice with an approved inhaled or injectable anesthetic.
Retrieve one mouse from the anesthetic chamber and place it in your hand to observe its respiration rate.
Position the mouse for intranasal instillation when the breathing rate is once every 2–3 s.
Familiarize yourself with the specific equipment for gaseous anesthesia before use.
Regulate the mouse’s breathing rate during anesthesia to ensure optimal timing for intranasal instillation.
Load the pipette with the agent set to be intranasally administered and set it aside until step 7.
Place the mouse on its back in the palm of your non-dominant hand.
Trace along the midline of the mouse, over the xyphoid process/sternum, up the throat, and onto the jaw and throat using your thumb.
Apply light pressure with your thumb during the tracing.
Place the mouse in your non-dominant hand carefully.
Ensure the mouse’s jaw remains tightly closed during administration.
Practice placing the mouse and applying thumb pressure on the jaw.
Observe the mouse's respiration to confirm proper positioning.
Position the supine mouse at a 60° incline with your thumb depressed.
Check the breathing rate of the mouse while maintaining pressure on the jaw.
Adjust your thumb positioning if necessary to maintain rhythmic breathing.
Hold the loaded pipette in your dominant hand and position it above the nares.
Depress the pipette plunger slowly to instill a droplet onto the mouse’s nares.
Wait for the mouse to inhale the droplet before administering the next one.
Maintain the supine mouse in a 60° position for another 2–3 breaths after inhalation to ensure liquid does not bubble back out of the nose.
Aspirate any observed bubbling liquid by pipette and re-administer as described.
Place your thumb on the mouse’s chest lightly if droplet has been efficiently inhaled, feeling turbulence with every breath.
Return the mouse to its cage and place it on its back to recover.
Soak the abdominal and thoracic regions with 70% ethanol to disinfect the area.
Make an incision into the abdomen, continuing towards the rib cage using surgical scissors and forceps.
Laterally displace the abdominal organs using forceps, exposing the abdominal artery.
Absorb the blood using sterile gauze.
Alternatively, collect blood directly from the artery using a 27G needle and syringe.
Dissect the liver from the diaphragm.
Perforate the thoracic diaphragm without touching the lungs.
Push the lungs medially with forceps or the flat side of surgical scissors to separate them from the rib cage.
Dissect superiorly through both lateral aspects of the rib cage towards the clavicles using surgical scissors.
Grip the ribcage with forceps.
Grasp the base of the mouse’s tail with one hand and pull the ribcage superiorly towards the head to expose the intact trachea.
Clean the exposed trachea if any residual bleeding is observed using sterile gauze.
Sharply dissect tissues in the throat region to expose the intact trachea.
Grip the most superior part of the trachea immediately inferior to the larynx.
Dissect the trachea with surgical scissors superior to where forceps are grasping the trachea.
Hold the trachea with forceps and gently pull distally while cutting away connective tissue along the ribcage.
Continue dissecting until the entire thoracic block is freed from connective tissue.
Place the thoracic block onto a piece of wax paper so the trachea can be laid straight and flat.
Pass the trachea through the loop of the prepared surgical suture.
Load a BAL needle with 250 μL of sterile, ice-cold PBS.
Insert the BAL needle into the opening of the trachea while guiding with forceps.
Position the needle approximately halfway down the length of the trachea.
Ensure the sharp, beveled end of the needle is concealed by polyethylene tubing to avoid puncturing the trachea.
Tighten the surgical suture around the trachea, securing it to the metal shaft of the needle.
Check the depth of the BAL needle in the trachea and ensure the alignment of the surgical suture just below the opening of the trachea on the metal shaft of the BAL needle.
Use forceps to hold the tracheal tissue in place if necessary.
Tie the suture as tightly as possible to prevent the trachea from slipping off the needle during the BAL procedure.
Lift the lungs off the wax paper with a syringe, supporting them so they do not freely hang by placing a finger underneath the lungs.
Hold the syringe vertically to align the trachea with the needle and avoid any visible kinks.
Gently depress the plunger of the syringe to inflate the lung lobes on both sides.
Adjust the angle of the BAL needle if necessary to ensure inflation of both left and right lobes.
Aspirate the instilled PBS by gently pulling back on the syringe plunger.
Massage the lungs gently while pulling back on the plunger to aid in fluid retrieval.
Adjust the positioning of the BAL needle if resistance is felt when pulling the plunger back.
Place the lungs back down on the wax paper and readjust the BAL needle positioning as needed.
Detach the syringe from the BAL needle and eject the recovered volume into a 1.5 mL collection tube.
Aspirate an additional 200 μL of ice-cold PBS with the same syringe.
Reattach the syringe to the BAL needle and repeat steps involving fluid aspiration, retrieval, and positioning adjustment.
Eject the recovered volume from the second instillation into the same 1.5 mL collection tube used previously.
Place the collection tube on ice.
Aspirate 300 μL of ice-cold PBS with the syringe used for conventional BAL.
Reattach the syringe to the BAL needle and repeat steps involving fluid aspiration, retrieval, and positioning adjustment for exhaustive bronchoalveolar lavage.
Repeat the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) procedure as per steps 35–37 and eject the recovered volume into a fresh 1.5 mL collection tube.
Instill two additional times with 300 μL of ice-cold PBS each time during BAL.
Eject the recovered volumes from the repeated instillations into the same 1.5 mL collection tube (totaling 900 μL).
Place the collection tube containing the recovered volume on ice after BAL is complete.
Dissect lung lobes using scissors and forceps and place them in pre-labeled 1.5 mL lung collection tubes filled with 750 μL of cell culture media.
Optional: Perform perfusion by injecting 5 mL of ice-cold perfusion buffer into the right ventricle of the heart through a 23G needle.
Monitor for visible blanching of the lung tissue to confirm successful perfusion, which should appear predominantly white/translucent due to removal of red blood cells (RBC).
Incubate all samples on ice until collection is complete to maximize cell viability.
Centrifuge the 1.5 mL collection tubes containing the conventional and exhaustive BAL fluid at 3,000 × g, 4°C, for 5 min in a tabletop microcentrifuge.
Visualize the cell pellets after centrifugation.
Transfer the supernatant from the conventional BAL fraction to a fresh 1.5 mL collection tube and store samples at -20°C.
Decant the supernatant from the exhaustive BAL fraction into liquid waste with a pipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet from the conventional BAL fraction in 200 μL of cell culture media.
Combine this cell suspension with the cell pellet from the exhaustive BAL fraction and resuspend.
Store samples on ice until required for downstream applications.
Enumerate cells and determine viability by trypan blue staining.
Mince lung tissue into smaller pieces using surgical scissors in a 1.5 mL lung collection tube.
Transfer minced lung tissue into a sterile 50 mL polypropylene tube.
Dispense 10 mL of lung digestion solution into the 50 mL polypropylene tube containing the minced lung tissue.
Incubate samples in a 37°C shaking incubator at 225 rpm for 1 hour.
Pour samples through a 100 μm nylon mesh basket filter into a fresh sterile 50 mL polypropylene tube after incubation.
Grind the digested tissue through the basket filter with the rubber end of a plunger from a 5 mL syringe.
Occasionally rinse the filter with ice-cold RPMI-1640 to wash cells through the filter while grinding.
Repeat step until all visible pieces of lung tissue have been ground through the filter.
Use a separate filter for each sample.
Centrifuge samples at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize the cell pellet after centrifugation.
Decant the supernatant in one motion into a liquid waste container.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of RBC lysis solution.
Add an additional 1 mL of RBC lysis solution to the sample.
Incubate samples for 2 min at 18°C–25°C, occasionally agitating by gently swirling the tubes.
Stop the lysis reaction by adding 40 mL of ice-cold PBS to each sample.
Filter samples through a 100 μm nylon mesh basket filter into a new sterile 50 mL polypropylene tube.
Centrifuge samples at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min after filtering.
Visualize the cell pellet, then decant the supernatant in one motion into a liquid waste container.
Leave the tube momentarily inverted on a stack of low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of complete cell culture media.
Place samples on ice.
Enumerate cells and determine viability by trypan blue staining.
Resuspend cells to a final concentration of 2 × 10^7 cells/mL for downstream flow cytometric analysis.
Add volume/concentration-adjusted BAL and lung mononuclear cells to a 96 well U-bottom plate.
Plate 5 × 10^5–2 × 10^6 lung mononuclear cells.
Plate 3–5 × 10^5 BAL cells.
Volume-adjust cells to 200 μL.
Calculate the volume of peptide pool stock needed using the formula [peptide pool stock] × (volume of peptide pool stock) = 2 μg/mL × 0.2 mL.
Prepare stimulants at a final volume of 50 μL per condition with cell culture media.
Add lung/BAL mononuclear cells to the 96 well U-bottom plate and mix with the stimulant.
Prepare a working solution of Brefeldin A as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 50 μL of Brefeldin A working solution to each well containing cell culture media.
Ensure the final volume in each well is 200 μL by adding more cell culture media if necessary.
Incubate the plate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 6 hours.
Centrifuge the plated cells at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes after incubation.
Visualize and decant the supernatant from each well by flicking the plate into a liquid waste container.
Leave the plate momentarily inverted on low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets with 200 μL of ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Perform at least one wash step with PBS prior to staining with amine reactive viability dyes as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Prepare the viability stain working dilution in PBS as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 50 μL of the viability stain working solution to each well containing samples, except the unstained control.
Incubate the samples at 18°C–25°C for 20 min, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold PBS to each well following incubation.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min after adding PBS.
Visualize cell pellets after centrifugation.
Decant the supernatant by flicking the plate in one motion into a liquid waste container.
Leave the plate momentarily inverted on a stack of low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Prepare the working dilution of Fc block and resuspend samples in 50 μL of the working solution.
Incubate samples for 15 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize cell pellets and decant the supernatant by flicking the plate in one singular motion into a liquid waste container.
Leave the plate momentarily inverted on a stack of low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Prepare Trm Master Mix #1.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of Trm Master Mix #1.
Incubate samples for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize the cell pellets and decant the supernatant.
Prepare Trm Master Mix #2.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of Trm Master Mix #2.
Incubate samples for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize the cell pellets, then decant the supernatant.
Resuspend samples in 100 μL of Cytofix/Cytoperm.
Incubate samples for 20 min at 4°C, protected from light.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize the cell pellets, then decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the samples in 200 μL of 1× Permwash solution.
Centrifuge the plate at 750 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Pause point: Resuspend fixed cell pellets in 200 μL of PBS and store at 4°C for up to 24 h.
Centrifuge the plate at 750 × g at 4°C for 5 min prior to proceeding with step 74e.
Visualize the cell pellets, then decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the samples in 200 μL of 1× Permwash solution.
Prepare Trm Master Mix #3.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of Trm Master Mix #3.
Incubate samples for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of 1× Permwash solution to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 750 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
After centrifugation, visualize the cell pellets.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend samples in 200 μL of FACs buffer.
Samples are now ready for downstream flow cytometric analysis.
Plate mononuclear cells into a 96 well U-bottom plate.
Adjust cell volume and concentration for sufficient data resolution on the flow cytometer.
Plate 5 × 10^5–2 × 10^6 lung mononuclear cells per well.
Plate 3–5 × 10^5 BAL cells per well.
Adjust cell suspension to a total volume of 200 μL.
Prepare FMO/isotype controls for each color used in the staining panel.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Visualize cell pellets after centrifugation.
Decant the supernatant by flicking the plate into a liquid waste container.
Invert the plate momentarily on low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets with 200 μL of ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Prepare the viability stain working solution in PBS as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 50 μL of the viability stain working solution to each well containing samples, except the unstained control.
Incubate the samples at 18°C–25°C for 20 minutes, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold PBS to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize cell pellets then decant the supernatant by flicking the plate in one singular motion into a liquid waste container.
Leave the plate momentarily inverted on a stack of low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Prepare the working dilution of Fc block and resuspend samples in 50 μL of the working dilution.
Incubate samples for 15 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize cell pellets then decant the supernatant by flicking the plate in one singular motion into a liquid waste container.
Leave the plate momentarily inverted on a stack of low-particulate wipes to remove additional supernatant.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of APC Master Mix #1.
Incubate samples for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well after incubation.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Decant the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of APC Master Mix #2.
Incubate samples for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Add 150 μL of ice-cold FACS buffer to each well after incubation.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Visualize the cell pellets after centrifugation.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend samples in 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Samples are now ready for downstream flow cytometric analysis.
